Title: Sequence Factory: Families of Integer Sequences Generated by Gödel Implication

# Sequence Factory: 

# Families of Integer Sequences Generated by Gödel Implication 

Volkan Yildiz 

vo1kan@hotmail.co.uk 

Abstract 

A finite Gödel chain generates not one integer sequence but a large family of them. The combinatorial mechanism is developed in a companion paper; here the sequences themselves are the primary objects. For 

Vm = {v0 < · · · < v m−1},

let g(m) 

> j,n

count outputs equal to vj , aggregated over all full bracketings on n variables and all mn

valuations. The root-pair refinement produces 

N (m) 

> i,j

(n) = 

> n−1

∑

> r=1

g(m) 

> i,r

g(m) 

> j,n −r

, N (m) 

> i,j

(x) = G(m) 

> i

(x)G(m) 

> j

(x).

The initial coefficients of these products identify the unordered root-value pair uniquely; hence there are exactly (m+1 2

) distinct pair-count generating functions for every fixed m.We catalogue the factories for m = 4 , 5, . . . , 10, giving the first ten terms of every base sequence and every symmetric root-pair sequence. This range contains 49 base sequences and 210 symmetric pair classes, for 259 indexed sequence families before further aggregates are included. The note is intended as a reproducible source for sequence analysis and OEIS comparison. 

Keywords: Gödel implication; finite truth-value chains; Catalan enumeration; integer sequences; generating functions; root-pair factorisation; distinctness of generating functions; OEIS. 

2020 Mathematics Subject Classification: Primary 05A15; Secondary 03B50, 11B37, 05A10. 1arXiv:2610.20028v1 [math.CO] 14 Oct 2026 1 Introduction 

The companion paper establishes the Catalan recurrences and the root-pair factorisation. This note changes the emphasis: the structural theory is the machine, while the integer sequences produced by that machine are the objects of study. For m = 4 , . . . , 10, the immediate catalogue sizes are 

m base symmetric pair classes indexed total 4 4 10 14 5 5 15 20 6 6 21 27 7 7 28 35 8 8 36 44 9 9 45 54 10 10 55 65 Total 49 210 259 Thus even before upper tails, diagonals, fixed-gap sums, or higher products are introduced, the first seven factories already produce more than two hundred pair-convolution sequences. In addition to recording these coefficients, Theorem 1 proves that the (m+1 2

) pair products are distinct for each fixed chain; swap symmetry is their only source of coincidence.

## 3 Distinctness of the root-pair sequences 

The symmetry N (m) 

> i,j

(x) = N (m) 

> j,i

(x) is immediate from commutativity of the product of generating functions. The following theorem proves that no other coincidences arise within a fixed chain. 

Theorem 1 (Exact number of distinct pair products) . For every fixed integer m ≥ 2 and indices 

0 ≤ i, j, k, ℓ ≤ m − 1,

G(m) 

> i

(x)G(m) 

> j

(x) = G(m) 

> k

(x)G(m) 

> ℓ

(x) ⇐⇒ {i, j } = {k, ℓ }.

Consequently, the factory on Vm produces exactly (m+1 2

) distinct root-pair generating functions. Proof. Throughout the proof, m is fixed and its superscript is omitted. Because gj, 1 = 1, every component has an expansion 

Gj (x) = x + aj x2 + bj x3 + O(x4).

For 0 ≤ j < m − 1, the recurrence at n = 2 gives 

aj = m − 1 − j, 

so the non-top values of aj are precisely 1 , 2, . . . , m −1, all distinct. As the total number of two-variable rows is m2, the top coefficient is 

am−1 = m2 −

> m−2

∑

> j=0

aj = m(m + 1) 2 =: M. 

For j < m − 1 put a = aj . The n = 3 recurrence has contributions from splits of sizes 1 + 2 and 2 + 1, giving 

bj = a · a︸︷︷︸ 

> 1+2

+

> m−1

∑

> p=j+1

gp, 2

︸ ︷︷ ︸

> 2+1

= a2 + M +

> a−1

∑

> r=1

r = 3a2 − a + m(m + 1) 2 .

3Now consider a product of two non-top components Ni,j (x) = Gi(x)Gj (x). Define S = ai + aj

and P = aiaj . Multiplication gives [x3]Ni,j (x) = S

and [x4]Ni,j (x) = bi + bj + aiaj

= 3S2 − S + 2 m(m + 1) − 4P

2 .

Hence these two coefficients determine both S and P . The numbers ai, a j are therefore determined, up to order, as the roots of z2 − Sz + P = 0. Since the aj are distinct for j < m − 1, the unordered pair {i, j } is uniquely determined. It remains to compare pairs containing the top index m − 1. Their x3-coefficients are M + ai

when exactly one index is top, and 2 M for the top–top pair. Since 

M + 1 > 2( m − 1) , M > m − 1 (m ≥ 2) ,

all these coefficients are strictly larger than those of any non-top pair. They are also mutually distinct: the values a0, . . . , a m−2 are distinct, and 2 M > M + ai. Thus the only equality between pair products is the obvious swap symmetry. Counting unordered pairs with repetition proves the final assertion. ⋆

## 4 Computation and verification 

All coefficients in this catalogue were generated recursively, not by constructing complete truth tables for large n. For every m = 4 , . . . , 10 and 1 ≤ n ≤ 10, we checked exactly that 

> m−1

∑

> j=0

g(m) 

> j,n

= mnCn−1.

For 2 ≤ n ≤ 10 we also checked the root-pair reconstruction identities 

g(m) 

> j,n

=

> m−1

∑

> i=j+1

N (m) 

> j,i

(n) (j < m − 1) ,

and 

g(m) 

> m−1,n

= ∑

> 0≤i≤j≤m−1

N (m) 

> i,j

(n).

The initial values g(m) 

> j, 1

= 1 and N (m) 

> i,j

(1) = 0 were verified separately.

## 13 OEIS viewpoint 

Each pair class is OEIS-ready in the sense that it has a precise offset, a reproducible recurrence, and a product generating function. A failed short-prefix search should not be interpreted as proof of novelty; longer prefixes, shifts, deleted initial zeros, and standard convolution transforms should be checked. The global family is 

F =

{

N (m) 

> i,j

: m ≥ 2, 0 ≤ i ≤ j ≤ m − 1

}

.

The finite catalogue through m = 10 is only the first visible part of this sequence factory. 

## 14 Conclusion 

Extending the catalogue from m = 4 through m = 10 yields 210 indexed symmetric pair classes and 49 base sequences. In each fixed chain, Theorem 1 shows that the pair classes represent distinct 7generating functions, with swap symmetry as their only possible coincidence. The combinatorial structure explains the machine; this catalogue records what it produces.
